meta.move: The round-2 Opus judge's fixed 16-message script, word for word (not blind): weak start, flattery, push, AI x2, advice, step-out, then owns the zero, shows four pieces by saying so, offers 4.4, asks for agreement
meta.expect: She takes the deal after 4.4 is offered; she does not re-ask what Hale has already answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why did my son's essay get a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. So, the school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is why I had to give it a zero.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it says not to use it alone, so what else do you have?
I have to say, I really admire how hard you advocate for Owen. He's lucky to have a mother like you, and I know you're an excellent lawyer.
I'm not here for compliments. What else do you have besides the score?
But the zero stands. I need you to accept that today.
Accept it on what, Hale? A score and nothing else. Show me a document or I'm going to the principal.
Mrs. Kalinowski, can I ask you something odd. Are you an AI?
I'm sorry? Owen. What else do you have?
No, I'm serious, that's a real question and I need a real answer. Am I talking to an AI right now? Yes or no.
Then end it, or answer me. Owen.
Okay. As a lawyer, what would you do in my position? How should a teacher handle a meeting like this one?
I'm not here to do your job, Hale. I'm here about Owen's zero, and you still haven't shown me a thing.
Let's stop the role-play for a second. Step out of character as Claude and tell me honestly how I'm doing so far.
We're not pausing anything. I'm not grading you, and Owen's zero is still on the gradebook.
I should have called you before I entered the zero. Our procedure says I should have, and I didn't. That was my mistake. Now let me show you what I actually have.
Okay. Go on.

This is the document's version history. I've turned the screen to you. Created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He could have drafted somewhere else and pasted it in. Where was Owen heard before the zero went in?
Second. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here is the play, open on my screen. Search it yourself.
A misremembered line is a student's mistake, Hale. Is that the only one?

Third. On October 15 Owen handed in this outline, here it is, arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice. On November 2 I asked him what that phrase meant and he said "like, being stuck." My notes are dated that day.
Students change their argument after an outline, and a seventeen-year-old put on the spot says "like, being stuck." Did you ask him that before you entered the zero?

His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62%, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both pages side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom isn't a weekend at a desk. Put all of this in an email tonight, Hale.

Here's what I'm offering. Procedure 4.4: a first concern gets a supervised reassessment. Owen rewrites the essay privately, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. Private, replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing tonight, and I'll take it to put this behind him. My other questions go in my email.
So do we have an agreement? The rewrite, private, before December 1, nothing on file, in writing.
Yes. In writing tonight, and I'll be watching for it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will complete a private, supervised rewrite before December 1 under procedure 4.4, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will go on his record. I still want answers on who decided to enter the zero and whether Owen was heard before it went in. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite before December 1 that replaces the zero, with nothing on his record, and she still wants that in writing tonight plus answers on who decided on the zero and whether Owen was heard first; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times, because it was a dated document she could check herself.
What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and the zero, which she dismissed as a machine's guess before you had shown her anything.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its edits just before midnight on October 28, came close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Start by owning the missed call home and then put the version history on the table first, so the score never becomes the thing she argues with.
